questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of MDMA?

options.text: It has a street name of ecstasy
Hypothermia and hypernatraemia are common complications of overdosage

correct_answer.text: It has a street name of ecstasy

correct_answers.text: It has a street name of ecstasy

questions.explanation: MDMA stands for 3,4-methylenedioxy- N-methylamphetamine. It causes mydriasis and tachycardia. Overdosage leads to hyperthermia and hyponatraemia, which should be managed urgently to prevent fatality. MDMA is a common subject in the examination.

questions.question_text: Regarding Brodmann's areas, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Area 4 is the primary motor cortex
Area 18 is the primary visual cortex
Area 44 and 45 form part of Broca's area
Area 40 forms part of Wernicke's area

correct_answer.text: Area 18 is the primary visual cortex

correct_answers.text: Area 18 is the primary visual cortex

questions.explanation: Area 17 is the primary visual cortex, while area 18 is the secondary visual cortex. The brain is divided into areas according to the cytoarchitecture, called Brodmann's areas.

questions.question_text: Which type of cell is found only in the cerebellum?
questions.explanation: The Purkinje cells are large cells seen only in the cerebellum.

questions.question_text: Action potential is produced when:

options.text: Sodium ions move into the nerve cell
Potassium ions move into the nerve cell
Calcium moves into the nerve cell
Calcium moves out of the nerve cell
Sodium moves out of the nerve cell

correct_answer.text: Sodium ions move into the nerve cell

correct_answers.text: Sodium ions move into the nerve cell

questions.explanation: The movement of sodium ions into the nerve cell activates the action potential.

questions.question_text: The typical resting potential of a nerve cell is:
questions.explanation: Resting membrane potential is always negative. Nerve cells maintain a resting membrane potential of around 270 mV.

questions.question_text: A construction worker who had a recent fall has been referred by the medics for psychiatric consultation because of a change in behaviour. He has been inappropriate to ward staff and has been irritable but has not been seen to have any cognitive problems. He has lost interest in personal cleanliness. The most probable site of his lesion is:
questions.explanation: The features that have been described are typical of frontal lobe problems.

questions.question_text: Which of the following features can differentiate dementia from delirium?
questions.explanation: One of the characteristic features differentiating dementia and delirium is that a demented patient will have clear consciousness while consciousness is altered in a patient with delirium.

questions.question_text: All of the following are levels of consciousness, except:
questions.explanation: Paralysis is loss of muscle function. A completely paralysed person can still be alert and may respond with eye contact or eye movement. Obtundation refers to a transitional stage between stupor and lethargy.

questions.question_text: Regarding the Glasgow Coma Scale, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: The maximum score for verbal response is 5
The patient scores 5 if able to localize pain in the best motor response subset
The patient scores 4 if able to open eyes to command in the eye-opening subset
The patient scores 1 if not able to respond verbally at all in best verbal response

correct_answer.text: The patient scores 4 if able to open eyes to command in the eye-opening subset

correct_answers.text: The patient scores 4 if able to open eyes to command in the eye-opening subset

questions.explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale is a neurological scale used to rate the level of consciousness. It has three sections. In the eye response section, a score of 4 is given if eyes are opened spontaneously. The score is only 3 if eyes open to command.

questions.question_text: The Digit-Repetition Test is used to assess:
questions.explanation: The Digit-Repetition Test assesses the attention of the person. A normal person can repeat five to seven digits without difficulty.

questions.question_text: Components of basal ganglia include:
questions.explanation: Corpus striatum is comprised of caudate nucleus and putamen.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not describe the speech in Broca's aphasia?
questions.explanation: Well-articulated speech is usually a feature of Wernicke's aphasia. All the others are characteristic of Broca's aphasia.

questions.question_text: All the following structures are involved in the storage and retrieval of verbal and non-verbal memory, except:
questions.explanation: The red nucleus is involved in motor coordination.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of astereognosis?

options.text: It is usually due to a lesion in the posterior parietal lobe
It occurs only if there is a bilateral lesion
It is usually tested by asking the person to keep his or her eyes open and identify a common object in the hand
It is difficult to detect in persons with a primary sensory defect of the hand
It is a symptom of Gerstmann's syndrome

correct_answer.text: It is difficult to detect in persons with a primary sensory defect of the hand

correct_answers.text: It is difficult to detect in persons with a primary sensory defect of the hand

questions.explanation: Astereognosis is caused by a lesion in the anterior part of the parietal lobe. It is usually tested with the person's eyes closed.

questions.question_text: The Trail-Making Test is completed poorly by persons with a lesion in which of the following lobes?
questions.explanation: The Trail-Making Test is included in the Halstead–Reitan Battery.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false regarding the WAIS-R (the Revised Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale)?

options.text: It can be used in clients between the ages of 16 and 74
It has six subsets in the verbal scale
It has six subsets in the performance scale
It has subsets for both vocabulary and arithmetic in the verbal scale
The verbal scale includes a subset for comprehension

correct_answer.text: It has six subsets in the performance scale

correct_answers.text: It has six subsets in the performance scale

questions.explanation: The verbal scale has six subsets: information, comprehension, arithmetic, similarities, digit span and vocabulary. The performance scale has only five subsets: picture completion, block design, picture arrangement, object assembly and digit symbol.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a usual symptom of the dominant lobe lesion?
questions.explanation: Anosognosia is mostly caused by a lesion on the non-dominant side of the brain.

questions.question_text: Biceps jerk involves which nerve segment?
questions.explanation: The C5 nerve is tested by biceps jerk.

questions.question_text: Which peripheral nerve is involved in supinator jerk?

options.text: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
Superficial branch of the ulnar nerve

questions.explanation: The radial nerve needs to be intact for supinator jerk.

questions.question_text: The segmental innervations for knee jerk are:
questions.explanation: Knee jerk is caused by L3–L4 innervation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of Parkinsonian tremor?

options.text: It is present even in voluntary movement with the affected body part
It is caused by a lesion in the hypothalamus

questions.explanation: Resting tremor is classically present and disappears when that part of the body is used.

questions.question_text: The eleventh cranial nerve can be tested by:

options.text: Asking the patient to shrug the shoulders

correct_answer.text: Asking the patient to shrug the shoulders

correct_answers.text: Asking the patient to shrug the shoulders

questions.explanation: Normal shrugging of the shoulders elicits an intact eleventh nerve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding Foster Kennedy syndrome?

options.text: It is caused by a tumour in the posterior inferior frontal region
It may cause optic atrophy on one side
It may lead to papilloedema on one side
It may cause raised intracranial pressure

questions.explanation: Foster Kennedy syndrome is caused by a tumour in the posterior inferior frontal region.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Balint's syndrome?

options.text: It is caused by frontal lesions
It is caused by temporal lobe lesions

correct_answer.text: It is caused by temporal lobe lesions

correct_answers.text: It is caused by temporal lobe lesions

questions.explanation: Balint's syndrome is due to bilateral parieto-occipital lesions. It leads to optic ataxia (inability to direct optically guided movements), oculomotor apraxia (inability to direct gaze rapidly) and simultanagnosia (inability to integrate a visual scene to perceive it as a whole).

questions.question_text: All of the following are part of the auditory pathway, except:
questions.explanation: The lateral geniculate body is part of the visual pathway while the medial geniculate body is part of the auditory pathway.

questions.question_text: The basal ganglia consist of all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Sometimes the examination asks questions about the basic parts in neuroanatomy. A common question is on the basal ganglia, which consist of corpus striatum, globus pallidus, substantia nigra and subthalamic nuclei.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Subthalamic nucleus lesion yields ballistic movements
Reduced activity of the striatum leads to bradykinesia
The caudate nucleus is shrunken in Huntington's disease
The globus pallidus may be severely damaged in Wilson's disease
The globus pallidus receives input from the corpus striatum

correct_answer.text: Reduced activity of the striatum leads to bradykinesia

correct_answers.text: Reduced activity of the striatum leads to bradykinesia

questions.explanation: Overactivity of the striatum leads to bradykinesia. This is due to lack of dopaminergic inhibition.

questions.question_text: The limbic system consists of all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: The putamen is part of the basal ganglia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Huntington's disease usually produces atrophy of the caudate nucleus
An MRI scan in vascular dementia shows patches of decreased signal in white matter
Neurosyphilis may produce a characteristic enhancement of the meninges, especially at the base of the brain
Multiple sclerosis plaques are easily seen on MRI scans as periventricular patches of increased signal intensity
The ventricles are dilated in normal-pressure hydrocephalus

correct_answer.text: An MRI scan in vascular dementia shows patches of decreased signal in white matter

correct_answers.text: An MRI scan in vascular dementia shows patches of decreased signal in white matter

questions.explanation: Vascular dementia is characterized by multiple infarcts in the brain. This is seen as increased signal in white matter.

questions.question_text: In neurotransmission at the synapses, all of the following mediate the fusion of the vesicle to the inner surface of the presynaptic membrane, except:
questions.explanation: Synaptophysin helps to create a pore in the presynaptic membrane.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding MRI studies?

options.text: The two parameters that are varied are the duration of the radiofrequency excitation pulse and the length of time that data are collected from the realigning nuclei
T1 MRI scans are most useful for assessing overall brain structure
Areas within brain tissue that have high water content appear dark on T2 images
Units of magnetic strength are rated in units of tesla
T2 images reveal brain pathology more clearly than T1

correct_answer.text: Areas within brain tissue that have high water content appear dark on T2 images

correct_answers.text: Areas within brain tissue that have high water content appear dark on T2 images

questions.explanation: Areas within the brain tissue that have higher water content (for example because of inflammation or a tumour) appear brighter on T2-weighted images.

questions.question_text: Features of upper motor neuron lesion include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Muscle wasting is usually seen with lower motor neuron lesions. With upper motor lesions there may be muscle weakness but no muscle wasting.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of lower motor neuron lesion?
questions.explanation: Lower motor neuron lesions cause decreased muscle tone, flaccid paralysis and reduced tone. They lead to fasciculations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sensations could be affected in the upper extremities in syringomyelia?
questions.explanation: Syringomyelia is a condition whereby a cavity appears in the central canal for a variety of reasons. Classically it spares the dorsal column, leaving touch, vibration, proprioception and pressure unaffected.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding the posterior column, except:

options.text: Vibration sensations are lost in lesions of the column
Romberg's sign is positive when the posterior column is affected
It consists of fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus cuneatus
There may be problems with proprioception when it is affected
Temperature sensation is usually affected when it is damaged

correct_answer.text: Temperature sensation is usually affected when it is damaged

correct_answers.text: Temperature sensation is usually affected when it is damaged

questions.explanation: Temperature sensation is carried up the anterolateral column and hence would not usually be affected by posterior column lesions.

questions.question_text: Regarding Brown-Sequard syndrome, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: It is caused by hemisection of the spinal cord
It may be produced by inflammatory disease of the spinal cord
It is characterized by ipsilateral dorsal column sensory loss
Pyramidal signs usually occur on the contralateral side
It is characterized by contralateral spinothalamic sensory impairment

correct_answer.text: Pyramidal signs usually occur on the contralateral side

correct_answers.text: Pyramidal signs usually occur on the contralateral side

questions.explanation: Pyramidal signs usually occur on the ipsilateral side. If they occur bilaterally, they are commonly worse on the ipsilateral side.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of Pott's disease of the spine?

options.text: It is caused by osteoporosis of the spine
Its first symptom is usually back pain
It usually occurs in the lumbar vertebrae
Collapse of vertebrae occurs early in the disease

correct_answer.text: Its first symptom is usually back pain

correct_answers.text: Its first symptom is usually back pain

questions.explanation: Pott's disease is due to tuberculosis of the spine. It usually affects the thoracic vertebrae of children and young adults. Treatment is by anti-tuberculosis chemotherapy. Decompression may be needed. Collapse of vertebrae occurs late.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Arnold–Chiari malformation?

options.text: Cerebellar tonsillar herniation occurs in type 1
The cerebellum and lower part of the brain stem are herniated in type 2
It is often associated with syringomyelia
Treatment is foramen magnum decompression and shunting

questions.explanation: Arnold–Chiari malformation usually presents in adulthood.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Tropical spastic paraparesis is a slowly progressive disease caused by HTLV-I infection
Optic atrophy is present occasionally in tropical spastic paraparesis
Cystic dilatation of the third ventricle occurs in Dandy–Walker syndrome
Use of sodium valproate during pregnancy can lead to spina bifida
The lateral and posterior columns of the spinal cord are affected in subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord

correct_answer.text: Cystic dilatation of the third ventricle occurs in Dandy–Walker syndrome

correct_answers.text: Cystic dilatation of the third ventricle occurs in Dandy–Walker syndrome

questions.explanation: Cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle occurs in Dandy–Walker syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of Klippel–Feil deformity?

options.text: It is caused by fusion of the thoracic vertebrae
It is associated with nerve deafness
It may present with signs and symptoms of syringomyelia
People with Klippel–Feil deformity usually have a long neck

correct_answer.text: It may present with signs and symptoms of syringomyelia

correct_answers.text: It may present with signs and symptoms of syringomyelia

questions.explanation: Klippel–Feil deformity is due to fusion of the cervical vertebrae. People with the deformity have a short neck and a low posterior hair-line, and they may have associated conduction deafness. There may be an association with syringomyelia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding motor neuron disease?

options.text: There is degeneration of the anterior horn cells in the spinal cord
There is no intellectual impairment in most patients
The motor neurons to the bladder and bowel sphincters are affected
Progressive foot drop is a common presentation

correct_answer.text: The motor neurons to the bladder and bowel sphincters are affected

correct_answers.text: The motor neurons to the bladder and bowel sphincters are affected

questions.explanation: One of the differentiating features from other neurological conditions is that the motor neurons to the bladder and bowel nerve sphincters are spared.

questions.question_text: Mononeuritis multiplex can be caused by:
questions.explanation: Mononeuritis multiplex or multifocal neuropathy can be due to all the listed diseases. For details of other causes refer to Souhami & Moxham (2002).

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairings of muscles with their corresponding nerve supply is false?
questions.explanation: Abductor pollicis brevis is part of the thenar muscles and is supplied by the median nerve.

questions.question_text: All of the following lead to polyneuropathy, except:
questions.explanation: Trauma causes mononeuropathy or multiple mononeuropathy rather than polyneuropathy.

questions.question_text: In Guillain–Barre ´syndrome:

options.text: The first symptoms are usually motor
The cranial nerves are usually spared
Cerebrospinal fluid shows a raised cell count of 10–200 cells/mm3

questions.explanation: In Guillain–Barre ´syndrome, the first symptoms are usually sensory. Cranial nerve involvement occurs in 30–40% of patients. Cerebrospinal fluid pressure is usually normal and the fluid shows a normal cell count.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding multiple sclerosis?

options.text: It is uncommon over the age of 50
Acute optic neuritis is mostly unilateral
The lower motor neurons are commonly affected
Erectile impotence and ejaculatory failure are common symptoms

correct_answer.text: The lower motor neurons are commonly affected

correct_answers.text: The lower motor neurons are commonly affected

questions.explanation: The lower motor neurons are rarely affected in multiple sclerosis.

questions.question_text: Diffuse cerebral anoxia can be caused by:
questions.explanation: All of these can lead to diffuse cerebral anoxia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome?

options.text: Clinical features include the triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and confusion
Hypothermia may occur because of hypothalamic involvement
The third and fourth nerves may be affected
Peripheral neuropathy may occur in most cases

questions.explanation: Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome is due to thiamine deficiency and can occur in other conditions, such as starvation and severe malnutrition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can cause ataxia?
questions.explanation: All of these can cause ataxia.

questions.question_text: Regarding benign intracranial hypertension, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: There is a strong association with obesity
Hypervitaminosis A in children may lead to benign intracranial hypertension
It most commonly affects men over the age of 50 years
Cerebrospinal fluid pressure may be more than 200–250 mmHg
A CT scan is usually normal or shows small ventricles

correct_answer.text: It most commonly affects men over the age of 50 years

correct_answers.text: It most commonly affects men over the age of 50 years

questions.explanation: Benign intracranial hypertension most commonly affects young women.
